card: Halts reindexing with a fatal error if the genesis block body read from external block files fails validation. When reindexing corrupted data with a valid genesis header but invalid payload, nodes previously crashed on a CheckBlockIndex assertion under -checkblockindex (default on regtest) or hung indefinitely in RPC warmup. The change adds an explicit fatal error check in ChainstateManager::LoadExternalBlockFile and a regression test.
changed_since_previous: Now includes the concrete 31-line patch; the implementation directly matches the prior description.
evidence: PR description: 'With -checkblockindex, the default on regtest, it aborts on an assert in CheckBlockIndex. Without it, it stays in RPC warmup.'
Author adds a test in test/functional/feature_reindex.py flipping a bit in the genesis block's coinbase locktime to trigger the issue, noting it reproduces the assertion on master.
problem: When reindexing block files where the genesis block body is corrupted but its header is intact, the header is added to the block index while the block is rejected. Subsequent headers are also added, leaving the index without an active chain; this causes an assertion failure in CheckBlockIndex under -checkblockindex (regtest default) or leaves the node hanging in RPC warmup indefinitely.

risk.why: A flaw in reindexing block validation logic could prematurely abort valid reindex operations or crash node startup.

scope_notes: Small focused change across validation.cpp and feature_reindex.py.
summary: Stops reindexing with a fatal error if the genesis block in disk storage has an intact header but an invalid body. It triggers an explicit fatal init error via GetNotifications().fatalError instead of continuing to read subsequent block headers when the genesis block fails validation.
